content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp scampi is a dish of large peeled shrimp sautéed in butter with garlic, lemon juice, and white wine, often finished with parsley. It features a bright aroma, a slightly tangy‑sweet flavor, and a tender seafood texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “scampi” comes from the Italian name for a type of sea‑crab, but in the U.S. the dish is traditionally made with shrimp.
The classic recipe uses only four ingredients: shrimp, butter, garlic, and wine.
It cooks quickly—usually 10‑15 minutes—making it a staple of fast‑service restaurants.
Scampi is commonly served over pasta, rice, or with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Variations add tomatoes, cream, or chili flakes for a different flavor profile.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Shrimp provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A 100‑g serving of shrimp contains about 99 kcal, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA in shrimp support heart and vascular health.

items.title: High in micronutrients
items.content: Shrimp are rich in selenium, zinc, and vitamin B12, important for immunity and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Astaxanthin, a natural antioxidant in shrimp, helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Shrimp are a common allergen; reactions can range from mild to life‑threatening.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so individuals with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: In some regions shrimp may contain heavy metals or antibiotic residues; choose reputable sources.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared scampi sauce often includes salt; people monitoring sodium intake should adjust accordingly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot shrimp scampi over pasta, rice, couscous, or with fresh bread. Garnish with chopped parsley, lemon wedges, and grated Parmesan for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw peeled shrimp in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Cooked scampi is best eaten within 24 hours; otherwise the sauce may separate. Freeze unused shrimp in a sealed bag for up to 3 months.
